events.text: William Dwight Whitney was born in Northampton, Massachusetts.
events.subject: self
events.quote: William Dwight Whitney was born in Northampton , Massachusetts on February 9 , 1827 .

events.text: Whitney entered Williams College at fifteen.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Whitney entered Williams College at fifteen

events.text: Whitney graduated from Williams College.
events.subject: self
events.quote: graduating in 1845

events.text: Whitney assisted his older brother Josiah Whitney on a geological survey of the Lake Superior region.
events.subject: self
events.object: geological survey of the Lake Superior region
events.quote: assisted his older brother Josiah Whitney on a geological survey of the Lake Superior region in 1849

events.text: Whitney left the United States to study philology and especially Sanskrit in Germany.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1850 , Whitney left the United States to study philology , and especially Sanskrit , in Germany .

events.text: Yale University offered Whitney a position as Professor of Sanskrit.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1853 , Yale University offered Whitney a position as Professor of Sanskrit

events.text: Whitney received his doctoral degree from the University of Breslau.
events.subject: self
events.quote: It was not until 1861 , however , that he received his doctoral degree from the University of Breslau .

events.text: Whitney served as secretary to the American Oriental Society.
events.subject: self
events.quote: served as secretary to the American Oriental Society from 1857

events.text: Whitney became president of the American Oriental Society.
events.subject: self
events.quote: until he became its president in 1884

events.text: The American Philosophical Society elected Whitney to membership.
events.subject: self
events.quote: The American Philosophical Society elected Whitney to membership in 1863 .

events.text: Whitney married Elizabeth Wooster Baldwin.
events.subject: self
events.quote: On August 28 , 1856 , Whitney married Elizabeth Wooster Baldwin .

events.text: Whitney died at his home on Whitney Avenue.
events.subject: self
events.quote: He died at his home , on Whitney Avenue , on June 7 , 1894 .

events.text: Whitney revised definitions for the 1864 edition of Websters American Dictionary.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Whitney revised definitions for the 1864 edition of Websters American Dictionary

events.text: Whitney became a founder and first president of the American Philological Association.
events.subject: self
events.quote: in 1869 became a founder and first president of the American Philological Association

events.text: Whitney became Yales professor of comparative philology.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the same year he also became Yales professor of comparative philology

events.text: Whitney gave instruction in French and German in the college until 1867.
events.subject: self
events.object: French and German in the college
events.quote: gave instruction in French and German in the college until 1867

events.text: Whitney gave instruction in the Sheffield scientific school until 1886.
events.subject: self
events.quote: in the Sheffield scientific school until 1886

events.text: Whitney wrote metrical translations of the Vedas and numerous papers collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series (1872–74).
events.subject: self
events.quote: collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series ( 1872–74 )

events.text: The Oriental and Linguistic Studies series ended in 1874.

events.quote: collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series ( 1872–74 )

events.text: Whitney was editor-in-chief of the first edition of the Century Dictionary, which appeared from 1889 to 1891.
events.subject: self
events.quote: he was editor-in-chief of the first edition of the respected Century Dictionary , which appeared from 1889 to 1891

events.text: The Century Dictionary's appearance ended in 1891.
